entries.title: Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light
entries.definitive_edition: Windows Steam release with available DLC packs

emulation.notes: Use native Windows for the main route. Original console hardware or backward-compatible Xbox hardware is only needed for historical platform comparison, not for unique archive content.

primary.version: Steam PC release with available DLC packs
primary.why: Windows is the highest-fidelity archive route: it is a native PC release, Steam carries the PC DLC packs, and no story or mission content forces a second platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Steam Windows version at native display resolution with the Steam DLC packs installed. Use the Feral Switch, iOS, or Android releases only if a modern portable route is preferred over capture fidelity.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Xbox Live Arcade console release at fixed console fidelity.
all_releases.reason: skip: historically important first console route, but Windows offers better capture control and there is no Xbox-only story or mission content.

all_releases.fidelity: Original PlayStation Network console release at fixed console fidelity.
all_releases.reason: skip: same core game family as Xbox 360/Windows with lower capture flexibility than the native PC route.

all_releases.fidelity: Native PC release with the best resolution and capture ceiling; the base game and available PC DLC packs are on Steam.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest-fidelity main route and the clearest currently documented DLC path for archive capture.

all_releases.fidelity: Touch/mobile route; Feral's later iOS release supports iPhone and iPad, controllers, and a full-game unlock.
all_releases.reason: skip: useful current portable option, but there is no iOS-exclusive content over Windows, and capture/control flexibility is lower than PC.

all_releases.fidelity: Touch/mobile route; Feral's modern Android release supports controller and keyboard/mouse options on compatible devices.
all_releases.reason: skip: current Android availability is valuable for access, but it does not beat Windows for archive capture and no Android-exclusive content exists.

all_releases.fidelity: Legacy tablet/mobile release.
all_releases.reason: skip: obsolete ecosystem with no unique content over the Windows route.

all_releases.fidelity: Historical browser/Chrome app route.
all_releases.reason: skip: browser delivery adds no exclusive content and is less practical for preservation than native Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Cloud-streamed release on a discontinued service.
all_releases.reason: skip: Stadia has shut down, so it is not a current preservation or play route and has no documented exclusive content.

all_releases.fidelity: Feral Interactive Switch collection release; convenient modern console and handheld route.
all_releases.reason: skip: current portable console bundle, but Windows remains the better capture-fidelity route and no Switch-exclusive content exists.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No platform-exclusive story, mission, or character content would force a secondary play segment; choose Windows for fidelity.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Switch and Feral mobile releases are useful modern ports, but they are alternative access routes rather than required content-completeness routes for this archive pick.

entries.title: Lara Croft and the Temple of Osiris
entries.definitive_edition: Windows Steam release with Season Pass/DLC

emulation.notes: Native Windows route; no emulator required.

primary.version: Steam PC release with Season Pass/DLC
primary.why: Windows is a launch platform, with official add-ons and Gold/Season Pass packages; Windows provides the highest capture ceiling while Switch/PS4/Xbox One/Stadia add no exclusive missions.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows Steam version with the Season Pass or individual DLC packs installed, at native display resolution. Use the Switch collection only if local co-op portability is the goal.

all_releases.fidelity: Native PC release with configurable resolution and the documented Steam DLC route.
all_releases.reason: primary: highest fidelity/capture ceiling and the Season Pass/DLC route covers the extra tomb and item packs.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console download release.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over the Windows Season Pass route.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console download release.
all_releases.reason: skip: no sourced exclusive content over the Windows Season Pass route.

all_releases.fidelity: Cloud-streamed release.
all_releases.reason: skip: Stadia is discontinued, and no Stadia-exclusive content is sourced.

all_releases.fidelity: Feral Interactive Switch collection release with local co-op and included DLC packs.
all_releases.reason: skip: convenient current console edition and includes the DLC packs, but Windows still has the higher capture ceiling.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The Windows Season Pass/DLC route covers the sourced extra content while keeping the best capture ceiling.

entries.remaster_caveats: The Switch collection is a useful modern console bundle, but it is not required for exclusive content and is not the primary fidelity route.

entries.title: Lara Croft Go
entries.definitive_edition: Steam desktop release updated through Mirror of Spirits

emulation.notes: Native Windows route; no emulator required. Mobile or console versions are optional historical comparisons.

primary.version: Steam desktop release updated through Mirror of Spirits
primary.why: Windows/Steam is the cleanest archive route: it has desktop capture controls, the PC release is on Steam, and the Mirror of Spirits chapter later arrived on Steam as a free update after its PlayStation time-exclusive window.
primary.how_to_play: Install the Steam Windows version, update it fully so Mirror of Spirits is unlocked, and capture at native desktop resolution.

all_releases.fidelity: Original touch mobile release.
all_releases.reason: skip: same core puzzle campaign family, with desktop Windows offering better capture control once updated.

all_releases.fidelity: Original touch mobile release.
all_releases.reason: skip: same core puzzle campaign family; no Android-only content over the updated Windows route.

all_releases.fidelity: Legacy Windows Phone release.
all_releases.reason: skip: obsolete mobile ecosystem and no unique content over the updated desktop route exists.

all_releases.fidelity: Original Windows app route before the Steam desktop release.
all_releases.reason: skip: same platform family, but the Steam Windows build has clearer update documentation for the final Mirror of Spirits chapter.

all_releases.fidelity: Console download release that received Mirror of Spirits during its time-exclusive window.
all_releases.reason: skip: Mirror of Spirits later arrived on Steam as a free update, so PS4 no longer needs a secondary play segment.

all_releases.fidelity: Portable PlayStation release that received Mirror of Spirits during its time-exclusive window.
all_releases.reason: skip: Mirror of Spirits later arrived on Steam as a free update, so Vita no longer needs a secondary play segment.

all_releases.fidelity: Native Steam desktop release with the best capture/control route and free Mirror of Spirits update support.
all_releases.reason: primary: updated Steam Windows covers the sourced final chapter while keeping desktop capture fidelity.

all_releases.fidelity: Native desktop Steam release on Mac.
all_releases.reason: skip: same Steam content family, but Windows is the selected archive capture route.

all_releases.fidelity: Native desktop Steam release on Linux.
all_releases.reason: skip: same Steam content family, but Windows is the selected archive capture route.

all_releases.fidelity: tvOS living-room release.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The PlayStation versions initially had Mirror of Spirits as time-exclusive content, but Steam later received the chapter as a free update, so the updated Windows route covers fidelity and completeness.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster caveat; the key version issue is the former PlayStation time-exclusive chapter, now covered by the Steam update.

entries.title: Lara Croft Reflections

emulation.notes: The iOS client was service-tied; iOS emulation or sideloading would not restore the shut-down server.

primary.why: All sourced release data points to iOS only, with a New Zealand/Australia soft launch and later server shutdown; no alternate platform or complete current release is documented.
primary.how_to_play: No normal current play route is available: document the game through preserved screenshots/video, a previously installed client, and source material because the servers shut down on August 5, 2014.

all_releases.fidelity: Original iPhone/iPad free-to-play card-battle client, now archival because the online service shut down.
all_releases.reason: primary: the only sourced platform; marked archival because the server shutdown prevents a normal complete playthrough today.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: There is no alternate release to trade fidelity against completeness; the issue is service shutdown and preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No remaster or current rerelease is sourced. The original online service shut down in 2014, so the entry is archival rather than practically playable.

entries.title: Lara Croft Relic Run
entries.definitive_edition: Current Android/iOS mobile build (Android selected for capture)

emulation.notes: Use native Android hardware where possible; Android emulators should only be used if Google Play compatibility and account access are intact.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Mobile native resolution on current Android hardware

primary.why: Android, iPhone, iPad, and Windows Phone releases exist; the current Android route is available via Google Play, while Windows Phone is obsolete and iOS/iPadOS add no exclusive content.
primary.how_to_play: Install the current Google Play version on a supported Android phone/tablet, sign in normally for the free-to-play service path, and avoid the Windows Phone release except for historical documentation.

all_releases.fidelity: Current official mobile route on scalable Android hardware.
all_releases.reason: primary: still has an official Google Play listing and no other platform has sourced exclusive game content.

all_releases.fidelity: Current iOS mobile route.
all_releases.reason: skip: same official mobile content family; Android is selected for the primary capture route.

all_releases.fidelity: Current iPadOS/tablet route.
all_releases.reason: skip: same official mobile content family with no sourced exclusive content over Android.

all_releases.fidelity: Legacy Windows Phone release.
all_releases.reason: skip: obsolete ecosystem and no sourced exclusive content over Android/iOS.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive stages, modes, or story content are documented; Android is selected for current official availability.

entries.remaster_caveats: Free-to-play mobile service state may change over time; preserve version/build information when capturing.
